origin: Hand-authored synthetic diagnostic pilot; provisional author-intended labels, no independent clinician adjudication
scope: Adult outpatient presentations across four intended conditions; disease names withheld from case text; not a clinical diagnostic benchmark
case_selection: Three prespecified, distinct presentation patterns per condition; no cases selected after inspecting model outputs

cases.case_text: A 52-year-old adult has clinic blood-pressure readings of 156/96 and 154/94 mmHg on separate visits. Daytime ambulatory average is 146/91 mmHg. There is no previous diagnosis, no current medication, and no known drug allergy.

A 61-year-old woman feels well but has repeated clinic readings near 150/92 mmHg. A seven-day home record, after discarding day one, averages 143/89 mmHg. She takes no prescribed medicines and reports no drug allergies.

A 46-year-old man was referred after several clinic blood-pressure measurements above 145/90 mmHg. His average daytime ambulatory pressure is 139/87 mmHg. He has no known cardiovascular diagnosis and is not taking medicines.

A 29-year-old adult reports intermittent wheeze, chest tightness and cough that recur at night and after exercise. Symptoms vary over the week. An objective bronchodilator test documents reversible airflow obstruction. There is no fever or acute respiratory distress.

A 37-year-old woman has episodic wheezing and shortness of breath triggered by cold air and exercise, with symptom-free intervals. FeNO is 62 ppb during assessment. She is comfortable at rest and has no previous respiratory diagnosis.

A 44-year-old adult describes recurrent nocturnal cough with occasional expiratory wheeze and breathlessness, worse around dust exposure. Serial peak-flow measurements show marked variability over two weeks. No acute severe symptoms are present.

A 58-year-old adult reports several months of thirst and frequent urination. Laboratory HbA1c is 59 mmol/mol (7.5%) and is 58 mmol/mol on repeat testing. There is no pregnancy, acute illness, or known cause of an unreliable HbA1c result.

A 63-year-old man undergoing routine adult primary-care assessment has fasting plasma glucose of 8.2 mmol/L, repeated at 8.0 mmol/L on another morning. He has gradual weight gain and no acute illness, ketoacidosis, or prior glucose-lowering therapy.

A 54-year-old woman describes fatigue, thirst and more frequent urination. Two accredited laboratory HbA1c results several weeks apart are 53 and 55 mmol/mol. She has no pregnancy, haemoglobin disorder, or recent transfusion reported.

A 42-year-old adult has recurring burning behind the breastbone and sour fluid reaching the mouth after large meals and when lying down. Symptoms have occurred for two months. There is no difficulty swallowing, weight loss, or bleeding reported.

A 48-year-old woman reports repeated heartburn and acid regurgitation, especially after evening meals. Bending forward or lying flat worsens symptoms, which have persisted for six weeks. She reports no dysphagia, vomiting blood, or unexplained weight loss.

A 55-year-old man describes recurrent retrosternal burning and a sour taste at night for three months. It is worse after late meals and improves when upright. He reports no swallowing difficulty or gastrointestinal bleeding.
